name: State the float tolerance and how it was chosen
body:
Tolerance: zero. Every value in the Nox trace equals the Rust trace's bit for bit, at 30, 60, 144 and 240 Hz (557, 554, 554 and 554 fixed steps).

How it was chosen: both engines write one line per fixed step (step number, feet position, velocity, grounded) through their shortest float formatting. Rust's `course_traversal` test writes `rust-<hz>hz.trace` when `LANTERN_TRACE_DIRECTORY` is set, and the Nox test writes `nox-<hz>hz.trace` the same way. The comparison parses each value and rounds it to f32 before comparing, because the two formatters can spell the same f32 differently (Rust's `0.000000059604645` against Nox's `5.9604645e-08`), and two decimal spellings of one f32 parse to different f64s. Rounded to f32, the largest difference measured was 0.

What made zero possible: the L4a review moved five divisions into glam's operation order (`ClampLengthMax3`, `MoveTowardsVector`, `TryStepUp` and both `separation / distance` sites), the Euler rotation follows glam 0.30.10's `from_euler` formula, and world matrices multiply from the root down, as Rust's recursion does. If a later change makes the traces differ, find the operation-order difference rather than raising the tolerance; a real tolerance would need its own reason on this card.

Rust traces are committed beside the Nox test in `engine/tests/world/the-course-matches-the-rust-trace-at-every-display-rate/`. Regenerate them with `LANTERN_TRACE_DIRECTORY=$PWD/engine/tests/world/the-course-matches-the-rust-trace-at-every-display-rate cargo test -p lantern-game-host --test course_traversal` after a change to the Rust controller, physics or course.
